newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal seen cutting repo rate 15-25 bp next wk.
newsitem.headline: Portugal seen cutting repo rate 15-25 bp next wk.

text.p: The Bank of Portugal is expected to cut its repo rate next week by between 15 and 25 basis points to reduce the differential with Spanish rates that followed Friday's 50 basis point cut in Spain's key money rate.

Five out of six economists and dealers contacted by Reuters said they expected a cut next week in the Portuguese repo rate, which now stands at 6.90 percent. A new commercial bank reserve period starts next Thursday.

"Now that parliament has passed the 1997 budget, the November inflation data has been published and Spain has cut its rate, the Bank of Portugal could change the repo rate," said Jose Carlos Andre of Banco de Comercio e Industria.
Pedro Azevedo of Banco Mello de Investimentos said he believed that the Bank of Portugal would cut the repo rate by up to 15 basis points.

"Since Fed chairman Alan Greenspan's anti-inflation warning, the markets are profit taking and closing positions, and we will see news about the EU stability pact bringing optimism to the markets," Azevedo said.
One of the reasons for an expected cut in the Portuguese repo rate is the large 65 basis points differential against the Spanish repo rate after Friday's 50 bp cut to 6.25 percent.
Economists say that such a differential is not justified when the inflation levels and fundamentals of the two economies are so similar.

Valentim Martins of Lisbon broker Siemca, the one analyst who doubted a Portuguese rate cut, said he doubted the Bank of Portugal would act before an agreement on 1997 public sector wages had been reached.
"The question of the public sector wages is very important because 1997 inflation is a vital consideration for Portugal's entry to economic and monetary union," he said.
"I think one of the reasons for the Spanish rate cut was that there is a public sector pay freeze in Spain," he added.
